page: Amazon Web Services c5n.18xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon 8124M processor operating at 3.4 GHz with x86_64 instruction set support, including AVX and AVX-512 extensions. The server provides 72 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 36 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The system includes 192.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, delivering approximately 2.67 GB of RAM per core.

Network throughput is a primary capability of this configuration, offering a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps. The instance contains zero discrete GPUs and features no local instance storage, requiring attached Amazon Elastic Block Store volumes for persistent data needs. In synthetic benchmarks, the machine achieves top-tier multi-threaded processing throughput, shown by strong results in PassMark CPU tests, extended instruction operations, and stress-ng multi-core execution.

Memory subsystem testing shows high cached read bandwidth of 3,704.68 GB/sec and uncached read bandwidth of 208.32 GB/sec, while write operations and single-core metrics fall within average industry percentiles. PassMark database tests show strong performance, though LLM text generation throughput remains limited without dedicated accelerator hardware. From an infrastructure cost perspective, the instance aggregates high compute density and extreme networking capability into a single dual-socket resource profile without requiring GPU premiums.

This hardware footprint is suited for network-intensive computational tasks, distributed high-performance computing clusters, parallel data transformation pipelines, and high-throughput network appliance emulation.
description: Amazon Web Services c5n.18xlarge is a high-bandwidth compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The system provides 72 dedicated vCPUs across 36 physical cores using an Intel Xeon 8124M processor clocked at 3.4 GHz, complemented by 192.0 GB of DDR4 memory. It offers a 100 Gbps baseline network interface without included local storage or GPU hardware. Benchmark results demonstrate strong multi-core computational throughput, high cached and uncached memory read bandwidth, and strong database transaction execution, balanced against average single-thread and memory write performance. Given its high vCPU count and high-throughput network fabric, c5n.18xlarge delivers balanced resource efficiency for parallel workloads that transfer heavy data volumes across network boundaries, such as high-performance computing clusters, parallel ETL processing, and large-scale distributed analytics.
